claim: SmolLM2's full 1.7B-parameter, ~11T-token pretraining run cost roughly 1e23 FLOPs, which the authors price at about $250,000 of GPU compute on 256 H100s.
stance_target: The compute budget required to train a 1.7B-class model to convergence, used as the upper anchor against which a 5x CMP 170HX box (~810 TFLOPS bf16 aggregate) is measured
scope_conditions: SmolLM2 base model, 1.7B parameters, ~11T training tokens, 256 H100 GPUs, nanotron framework
quoted_support: We trained the model on 256 H100s using the nanotron framework... Such on-the-fly rebalancing is a promising approach for large-scale training runs which can be sufficiently costly (around 1e23 FLOPs, or $250,000 USD worth of GPU compute for SmolLM2) to preclude running multiple full-scale training runs.

claim: SmolLM2's data-ablation configuration — 1.7B parameters, sequence length 2048, global batch of approximately 2 million tokens, 350B training tokens per ablation — is a published, working small-scale pretraining recipe, not a toy setting.
stance_target: The repo's claim that a ~1B-trainable model at 1M-token global batches is a legitimate experimental scale rather than a degenerate one
scope_conditions: SmolLM2 dataset ablation models, Llama architecture, GPT-2 tokenizer, cosine LR 3.0e-4
quoted_support: We trained 1.7B parameter Transformers (Vaswani et al., 2017) based on the Llama architecture (Touvron et al., 2023), with a sequence length of 2048, a global batch size of approximately 2 million tokens, the GPT-2 tokenizer (Radford et al., 2019), and a cosine learning rate schedule (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2016) with a learning rate of 3.0 x 10-4. Each dataset ablation model is trained on 350B tokens randomly sampled from the full dataset.

claim: FineMath is released in two sizes that bracket a small-run data budget: FineMath4+ at 10B tokens / 6.7M documents and FineMath3+ at 34B tokens / 21.4M documents.
stance_target: Whether the repo's 9B-token data mix can source a math component of the intended size from an openly licensed dataset
scope_conditions: FineMath release, Common Crawl derived, English, decontaminated against GSM8K/MATH/MMLU
quoted_support: Ultimately, we developed multiple variants of FineMath, including FineMath4+ (10B tokens, 6.7M documents) which retains only samples with scores of 4-5 and FineMath3+ (34B tokens, 21.4M documents) which includes scores 3-5.

claim: FineMath4+ delivers a 2x improvement on GSM8K and a 6x improvement on MATH relative to InfiMM-WebMath in the authors' annealing ablations, showing that classifier threshold choice dominates dataset size for math data.
stance_target: That data curation quality, not raw token count, is the load-bearing variable in a small-scale pretraining run
scope_conditions: Annealing ablations on 1.7B Llama-architecture models, 60B math tokens, GSM8K and MATH benchmarks
quoted_support: All FineMath subsets consistently outperform OWM and InfiMM-WebMath on GSM8K, MATH, and MMLU-STEM. FineMath4+ achieves a 2x improvement on GSM8K and a 6x improvement on MATH compared to InfiMM-WebMath, demonstrating the importance of retaining high-quality mathematical content with reasoning.

claim: Stack-Edu is a ~125B-token filtered subset of StarCoder2Data covering the 15 largest programming languages, produced by 15 language-specific StarEncoder classifiers trained on Llama3-70B-Instruct educational annotations.
stance_target: Whether the repo's 9B-token mix can source a code component from an openly released, size-adequate dataset
scope_conditions: Stack-Edu release, 15 languages, threshold 3 binary classification, F1 > 0.7 for most languages
quoted_support: We then trained 15 language-specific classifiers using the StarEncoder model (Li et al., 2023a) on synthetic annotations generated by Llama3-70B-Instruct (Dubey et al., 2024) (prompt in Appendix D.1), which rated the educational quality on a scale from 0 to 5... The resulting Stack-Edu dataset contains ~125B tokens across its 15 languages.

claim: Educational filtering of code cuts the corpus by roughly 3-4x per language while improving benchmark scores: Python drops 50.6B to 21.8B tokens with HumanEval rising 20.7 to 25.6, and C++ drops 69.7B to 16.0B with MultiPL-E rising 16.7 to 24.8.
stance_target: That aggressive quality filtering is a net win even at small scale, where token budget is the binding constraint
scope_conditions: Stack-Edu ablations, top 4 languages by size, HumanEval for Python and MultiPL-E for the rest
quoted_support: Filtering with a threshold of 3 improved performance across most languages while maintaining sufficient data, although Java performed better with threshold 2... Python 50.6 [B tokens] -> 21.8, MultiPL-E 20.7 -> 25.6; C++ 69.7 -> 16.0, MultiPL-E 16.7 -> 24.8.

claim: SmolLM2 extended context from 2k to 8k by continuing from an intermediate stage-4 checkpoint with RoPE base 130k and a mixture containing 40% long documents (>=8k tokens), rather than pretraining at 8k from the start.
stance_target: The repo's premise that long-context capability is added as a distinct late training stage, so a 32k experiment on the CMP 170HX box can be scoped as a stage rather than a full run
scope_conditions: SmolLM2 context-length extension, intermediate checkpoint before the final 75B tokens
quoted_support: we followed standard practice (Gao et al., 2024) and extended the context length from 2k to 8k tokens, by taking an intermediate checkpoint from stage 4 (before the final 75 billion tokens of training) and continuing training with a different data mixture and a RoPE value of 130k. The mixture was adjusted to include 40% long-context documents (8k tokens or more) sourced from DCLM (10%), FineWeb-Edu (10%), and the books subset of Dolma (20%).
numbers: final 75B tokens excluded from the checkpoint

claim: SmolLM2's four-stage mixture shifts from 90% English web in stage 1 to 58% web / 24% code / 14% math / 4% textbooks by stages 3-4, i.e. specialised data is introduced late to avoid dilution.
stance_target: Whether a multi-stage mixture schedule is required for a small-model run, which affects how many separate training runs the box must support
quoted_support: Stage 1 ... 90% English Web, 10% StarCoderData/Stack-Edu ... Stage 4 ... 58% English Web, 24% StarCoderData/Stack-Edu, 14% OWM/InfiMM-WebMath/FineMath, 4% Textbooks.

claim: FineMath's construction required re-extracting 7.7B URLs and processing 7.1B pages (6.5T tokens) before filtering down to 34B tokens, so the CPU-side data pipeline cost dwarfs the GPU training cost for a small math component.
stance_target: The repo's data-pipeline claim that preprocessing is a separate, CPU-bound cost centre that must be budgeted independently of GPU training
scope_conditions: FineMath curation pipeline, Common Crawl WARC extraction with Resiliparse and the OWM pipeline
quoted_support: From the Common Crawl index, we retrieved a total of 7.7B URLs belonging to this list of domains: 5.7B identified by our classifier, 0.6B from OWM, and 1.3B from InfiWebMath. We then re-extracted all identified pages using the OWM pipeline, preserving LaTeX formatting and removing all-boilerplate pages, yielding 7.1B pages containing 6.5T tokens.

claim: The SmolLM2 tokenizer has a 49,152-token vocabulary trained on a 70% FineWeb-Edu / 15% Cosmopedia-v2 / 8% OpenWebMath / 5% StarCoder-Data / 2% StackOverflow mixture.
stance_target: Vocabulary-size choices that affect embedding-table memory on 64 GB cards
quoted_support: We used the tokenizer from Allal et al. (2024), which has a vocabulary size of 49,152 tokens and was trained on a mixture of 70% of FineWeb-edu, 15% Cosmopedia-v2, 8% OpenWebMath, 5% StarCoder-Data and 2% StackOverflow.
